Below is a “starter kit” you can adapt depending on your interests, budget, and how long you’re willing to stay. I’ve broken it into three sections: 1. **Quick‑start checklist** – what you’ll need before you leave. 2. **Sample itineraries** – two options (short & extended), plus a few “add‑on” ideas. 3. **Practical tips** – money, transport, food, culture, safety, and more. Feel free to mix and match! --- ## 1️⃣ Quick–Start Checklist | Item | Why It Matters | |------|----------------| | Passport + Visa (if required) | France requires passports valid at least 90 days beyond arrival. EU/EEA citizens don’t need visas. Check Schengen rules if you’re from outside Europe. | | Travel insurance | Covers health emergencies, cancellations, lost luggage. | | Credit cards + cash (€) | Most places accept card; keep €50‑€100 in cash for markets, cafés, metro tokens. | | Power adapter (Type C/F) | French sockets are 230V, 50Hz. | | Comfortable walking shoes | You’ll walk a lot—Paris streets aren’t always flat. | | Light rain jacket / umbrella | Weather can change quickly. | | Reusable water bottle | Stay hydrated while exploring. | > **Tip:** Download offline maps (Google Maps, Citymapper) so you won’t rely on data roaming. --- ## 2️⃣ Sample Itineraries ### A. Short Trip (Weekend – 3 Days) | Day | Morning | Afternoon | Evening | |-----|---------|-----------|--------| | **Day 1** | Arrive → Hotel check‑in
Walk along Seine, cross Pont des Arts | Visit Notre‑Dame & Île de la Cité
(free entry) | Dinner in Le Marais (try falafel or duck confit)
Night stroll around Place des Vosges | | **Day 2** | Breakfast at Café de Flore (Saint‑Germain)
Visit Luxembourg Gardens | Lunch at Rue Cler market
Explore Musée d’Orsay (book ticket online) | Sunset cruise on the Seine (Bateaux Mouches) | | **Day 3** | Early morning climb Eiffel Tower (skip line via skip‑the‑line app)
Brunch at nearby café | Walk through Champs‑Élysées, Arc de Triomphe
Shopping in Galeries Lafayette | Departure | *Estimated daily spend:* €120‑150 (mid‑range dining, museum passes, occasional taxi). --- ### B. Extended Trip (Weeklong – 7 Days) #### *Base*: Hôtel du Palais Royal (Marais) – centrally located, easy access to Metro Line 8 & 9. | Day | Activity Highlights | Notes | |-----|--------------------|-------| | **Day 1** | Arrival, settle in, evening walk to Notre‑Dame | Get familiar with neighborhood | | **Day 2** | Louvre Museum (early opening 10am)
Lunch at Café Marly | Book timed entrance slot | | **Day 3** | Sacré-Cœur & Montmartre hilltop
Picnic at Square Louise Michel | Bring baguette, cheese, wine | | **Day 4** | Versailles Palace & gardens (day tour) | Reserve early, bring sunscreen | | **Day 5** | Day trip to Giverny (Monet’s garden) OR Champagne region (Reims) | Choose based on interest | | **Day 6** | Explore Canal Saint-Martin, trendy boutiques
Dine at L’As du Fallafel | Try vegan falafels | | **Day 7** | Free day: choose between Disneyland Paris, Catacombs, or a culinary workshop (e.g., pastry making) | Pack light bag for flexibility | *Optional add-ons:* Wine tasting in Bordeaux, bike rental for cycling along riverbanks, guided street art tour in Belleville. --- ### C. Budget Traveler (Low Cost – 5 Days) | Day | Plan | Approximate Cost | |-----|------|------------------| | **Day 1** | Hostel dormitory (~€25/night)
Free walking tour (tip-based) | €30 total | | **Day 2** | Free attractions: Notre‑Dame, Sainte-Chapelle (pay only for special exhibitions)
Café lunch ~€12 | €45 | | **Day 3** | Public park picnic (buy groceries at supermarket)
Metro day pass €14.60 | €20 | | **Day 4** | Museums with free admission on first Sunday of month (Louvre, Orsay) | €0 | | **Day 5** | Last-minute souvenir hunt in Marché aux Puces de Saint-Ouen | €15 | Total estimated spending: €140‑170 excluding flights. --- ## 3️⃣ Practical Tips ### Transport Within Paris | Mode | How to Use | Pros | Cons | |------|------------|------|------| | Métro | Buy single tickets (€1.90) or a carnet of 10 (€17.70) | Fast, covers most sites | Can get crowded during rush hour | | RER trains | For suburbs & airports | Cheaper than taxis | Requires separate fare | | Bus | Unlimited rides with Navigo Week Pass (€22.80) | Scenic routes | Slower due to traffic | | Vélib' bikes | Rent for hourly/daily rates | Eco-friendly, great exercise | Limited availability in winter | | Walking | Many sights cluster together | Best way to soak atmosphere | Wear comfortable shoes | > **Pro tip:** Grab a **Navigo Découverte** weekly pass (€22.80) if you’ll be traveling frequently—it gives unlimited rides across all modes (MRT, bus, tram, RER) for one calendar week. ### Money Management - Keep small bills handy for metro tokens, vending machines, cafés. - Avoid exchanging money at airport kiosks—they offer poor rates. Instead, withdraw from ATMs after paying fees once. - Use contactless payments where possible; they’re widely accepted. ### Dining Etiquette - Restaurants often have a service charge (“service compris”) already added to bill. If not, round up 5‑10% as tipping gesture. - Order à l’heure (at table) rather than standing at counter unless specified. - Try regional specialties: croissants, escargot, coq au vin, macarons. ### Cultural Do's & Don’ts | Do | Don't | |---|---| | Speak basic French greetings ("Bonjour", "Merci") | Assume everyone speaks English | | Respect quiet hours (nighttime, especially in residential areas) | Loud conversations late at night | | Take photos inside churches only when permitted | Flash photography in historic interiors | | Carry ID (passport) when visiting museums or hotels | Forget passport at hotel front desk | ### Safety & Health - Pickpocketing common in tourist hotspots (Notre‑Dame, Louvre, metro stations). Keep wallets in front pockets or zipped bags. - In case of emergency, dial 112 (EU-wide). - COVID‑19 guidelines may still apply; carry mask and hand sanitizer. ### Packing List (Compact) | Category | Items | |----------|-------| | Clothing | Lightweight layers, waterproof jacket, comfortable sneakers, dressier outfit for evenings | | Toiletries | Toothbrush, toothpaste, deodorant, minimal makeup | | Electronics | Phone charger, power bank, universal plug adaptor | | Documents | Passport, copies of reservations, travel insurance | | Miscellaneous | Small backpack/daypack, reusable water bottle, notebook | --- ## Final Thought Paris offers endless ways to tailor your experience—from luxury stays overlooking the Seine to cozy hostels tucked away in charming arrondissements. By planning ahead, leveraging public transit, and embracing both iconic landmarks and off‑beat neighborhoods, you’ll create memories that last far longer than the trip itself. Bon voyage!
message.reasoning:
The user wants a plan for a trip to Paris. We need to provide details like itinerary, travel tips, places to visit, accommodation suggestions, transportation within city, etc.

We can ask clarifying questions? But likely we just give general plan. Provide day-by-day schedule with recommended activities and times, mention budget categories, maybe include some hidden gems. Also mention best time to visit, visa info, currency exchange, safety tips, packing list. Could also suggest local cuisine spots, museums, parks, shopping districts. Maybe propose optional tours or experiences (wine tasting, cooking class). Suggest how many days based on typical length. Provide sample itineraries for different durations: short weekend vs week-long.

Also could incorporate flight booking advice, but not necessary. Might want to recommend using public transport (metro) over taxis; use Navigo pass. Mention buying tickets online for Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Montmartre. Include suggestion about staying near central location like Marais, Latin Quarter, Saint-Germain-des-Prés. Provide approximate cost per day.
